question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with higher speeds?
options: a:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,c:Are not affected by vehicle speed.
note: As your speed increases, both your stopping distance and the force of any crash increase. You need more distance to react and brake, and the impact is much more severe at higher speeds, so you should leave a larger following distance as you go faster.

question: How should you drive just after it begins to rain?
options: a:Avoid making turns and stops at high speed.,b:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: When rain first begins, oil and dirt on the road mix with water and make the surface very slippery. You should slow down and avoid fast turns or sudden stops so your tires can maintain traction and you have better control of the vehicle.

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed so:
options: a:Other drivers have space in front of the truck when they need to slow down.,b:The truck driver has room to stop the vehicle safely.,c:Other drivers can merge onto the freeway more easily.
note: Large trucks are heavy and need a much longer distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver enough room to slow or stop safely, reducing the risk of a rear-end collision if traffic suddenly changes.

question: Which statement about legal and over-the-counter drugs is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many prescription and over-the-counter medicines, such as cold, allergy, and sleep medications, can cause drowsiness or slow your reactions. Even if a drug is legal, it can still impair your driving, and it is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

question: In fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights so you can see and be seen without creating extra glare. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see, while low beams aim light down toward the road and improve visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:
options: a:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.,b:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,c:Both of the above.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks, and to all traffic already circulating inside the roundabout. Vehicles in the roundabout have the right-of-way over entering traffic.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Check your mirrors frequently to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you. Regular mirror checks help you spot fast-approaching vehicles, tailgaters, and changing traffic conditions so you can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection but are not in the correct lane to make your intended turn, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next intersection to make the turn.,b:Signal the direction you want to go and wait for a gap.,c:Stop and wait until the way is clear before turning.
note: If you are not in the correct lane for your intended turn, continue straight and make your turn at the next intersection from the proper lane. Turning from the wrong lane is unsafe and often illegal.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain or fog, use low-beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can make it harder to see.

question: How should you adjust driving on gravel or dirt surfaces?
options: a:Your tires grip better than on pavement.,b:You have less traction than on pavement, so slow down.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: On gravel or dirt, your tires have less traction and your stopping distance increases. Slow down, avoid sudden steering or braking, and increase your following distance to maintain control.

question: During adverse weather, how should you steer and brake?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In rain, snow, ice, or other poor conditions, sudden steering or hard braking can cause a skid. Use gentle, smooth steering and gradual braking so your tires keep traction and you maintain control of the vehicle.

question: What is the best method to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.
note: The best way to avoid dangerous situations is to stay aware of everything around your vehicle. Check ahead, to the sides, and behind you frequently so you can spot hazards early and adjust your speed or position before they become emergencies.

question: How can you reduce glare from oncoming headlights?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stay focused on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams at them.
note: When oncoming headlights cause glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This keeps you in your lane without staring directly into the bright lights, which can temporarily blind you.

question: What do "No passing zone" signs indicate?
options: a:To maintain a steady speed.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To speed up slightly.
note: A “No Passing Zone” sign means you must not pass other vehicles in that area. These zones are placed where visibility, curves, hills, or other conditions make passing unsafe, so you must stay in your lane until the restriction ends.

question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield to pedestrians and any traffic that has the right‑of‑way before you enter the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you travel?
options: a:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:At the posted speed limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions. This may be lower than the posted speed limit when visibility is poor, the road is wet or icy, or traffic is heavy. You may never exceed the posted speed limit, even if other drivers are going faster.

question: What is the only proven method to eliminate alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to break down and eliminate alcohol. Your liver can process only a certain amount per hour, and nothing you eat, drink, or do—such as coffee, a cold shower, or exercise—will speed this up. You must wait until your body has had enough time to metabolize the alcohol before driving.

question: A double solid yellow centerline indicates that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. You may cross only when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle from either direction.

question: Which headlights should be used in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Fog lights only.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air, creating glare and making it harder to see. Low beams provide better forward visibility and make your vehicle more visible to others without causing excessive glare.

question: How should you enter the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up.,b:Use the shoulder to get up to traffic speed.,c:Speed up and enter only after identifying a gap in traffic.
note: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you must adjust your speed on the ramp and enter only when you see a safe gap in traffic. Do not drive on the shoulder to gain speed. Yield to interstate traffic and merge smoothly when there is enough space.

question: What does Tennessee's Implied Consent Law require of drivers?
options: a:If requested, you must submit to a test for alcohol or drugs.,b:Traffic laws apply even without signs at intersections.,c:You may refuse tests for alcohol or drugs without consequence.
note: Tennessee’s Implied Consent Law means that by driving on Tennessee roads, you have already agreed to take a chemical test (breath, blood, or urine) if a law enforcement officer lawfully requests it. You may refuse, but that refusal brings automatic penalties such as license suspension, separate from any DUI charge.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane on water you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,b:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,c:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. You should ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not brake hard or make sudden steering movements, because that can cause a skid. Once you feel the tires regain traction, you can brake gently if needed.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and not brake.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: If a tire blows out or goes flat suddenly, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and ease your foot off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down gradually without hard braking, then gently apply the brakes when you have control and can move safely off the road. Hard or sudden braking can cause you to lose control, especially at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you come to a complete stop?
options: a:Where there is a red traffic light.,b:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must come to a complete stop at a steady red traffic light and at a flashing red light, just as you would at a stop sign. You also must stop whenever a police officer directing traffic orders you to stop, even if the traffic signal would otherwise allow you to go. Obeying traffic signals and lawful orders from officers is required in all states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do first before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Before stopping for a signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know what traffic is doing behind and around you. This helps you brake smoothly and gives drivers behind you time to react. After checking, ease off the accelerator and apply steady pressure to the brake pedal to come to a controlled stop.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:Inconvenience drivers.,b:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
note: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to guide traffic safely around or through construction areas and to keep vehicles out of hazardous work zones, protecting both drivers and workers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,b:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.,c:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward to check your blind spot. Even with mirrors, blind spots still exist, so you must turn your head to be sure the lane is clear.

question: When driving through work zones you should:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
note: In work zones, you must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Workers, equipment, and changed traffic patterns can appear unexpectedly, so extra caution and reduced speed are essential.

question: What is the minimum jail sentence upon a second DUI conviction?
options: a:Five days in jail.,b:20 days in jail.,c:45 days in jail.
note: Penalties for a second DUI conviction vary by state; there is no single nationwide minimum jail sentence of 45 days. Many states set different mandatory minimums, and some allow alternatives or enhanced penalties based on circumstances. Always study your specific state’s DUI laws for accurate penalty information.

question: Under low-visibility conditions caused by fog you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility. Slow down so you have more time to react, and if visibility becomes very poor, pull off the road to a safe location and wait until conditions improve.

question: After signaling and matching speed when entering the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.
note: When entering an interstate, you use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to find a safe gap in traffic, signal, adjust your speed to match the flow, and then merge smoothly into that gap. You do not have the right-of-way; freeway traffic is not required to move for you, so you must merge carefully only when it is safe.

question: Which of these is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment,b:Both of the above,c:Tailgating another vehicle.
note: Work zones are high-risk areas with narrowed lanes, changing patterns, and workers close to traffic. Following too closely (tailgating) reduces your time to react to sudden stops, and failing to watch carefully for workers and equipment increases the chance of a collision. Both behaviors are dangerous and should be avoided by slowing down, increasing following distance, and staying alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but traffic ahead blocks the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,b:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: A green light allows you to proceed only if the intersection is clear. You must not enter if traffic ahead prevents you from driving all the way through, because stopping in the intersection can block cross traffic and is illegal in many jurisdictions. Wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to clear the intersection completely.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Increase the volume of your radio.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,c:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
note: Fatigue greatly slows your reaction time and can lead to microsleeps, where you briefly fall asleep without realizing it. Turning up the radio or speeding does not restore alertness and can be dangerous. The safe choice is to get off the road at a safe place, such as a rest area or parking lot, and take a short nap or rest before continuing.

question: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line means:
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.,b:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,c:Vehicles in both directions may pass.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When one side is solid and the other is broken, only drivers next to the broken line may pass, and only when it is safe and legal. Drivers next to the solid line must not cross it to pass because it indicates that passing from that side is prohibited.

question: If there is a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline, what does that indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Traffic light ahead.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you are not allowed to pass other vehicles. It marks a no‑passing zone for your direction of travel, usually because of limited visibility or other safety concerns.

question: What is meant by 'distracted driving'?
options: a:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving, including taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off the driving task. Common examples are texting, eating, or adjusting controls while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection instructs drivers to:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down, look carefully for other traffic, and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop unless it is necessary for safety or to yield to other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while the traffic light is green, you should:
options: a:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the officer.,c:Obey the traffic signal.
note: Directions from a police officer override traffic signals and signs. If an officer signals you to stop, you must obey the officer even if the traffic light is green, because they may be managing a hazard or special situation.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you NOT take?
options: a:Applying your brakes.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel so you can control the vehicle, press your head firmly against the head restraint, and be ready to apply the brakes to avoid being pushed into another vehicle. You should not let go of the steering wheel, because you could lose control after impact.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness will:
options: a:Help you be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness, like alcohol and many drugs, slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment. A drowsy driver is less able to notice hazards and make safe decisions, which greatly increases crash risk.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is failing, it can cause:
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Your vehicle’s suspension system helps keep the tires in contact with the road and stabilizes the vehicle. When the suspension is failing, the car may bounce excessively, lean or sway in turns, and feel unstable, all of which can cause serious vehicle control problems.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway you should:
options: a:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance and acceleration lane to check traffic, signal, and increase your speed to match the flow of traffic. Merge smoothly when there is a safe gap; stopping on the ramp is dangerous except in an emergency or if traffic is stopped.

question: A driver's license may be suspended or revoked for:
options: a:Fraudulently altering a driver license.,b:Frequent convictions resulting in 12 or more points on a driving record.,c:Both of the above.
note: Licenses can be suspended or revoked for serious offenses such as fraud or accumulating excessive points from violations.

question: Which statement about alcohol and intoxication is incorrect?
options: a:As weight increases, more alcohol is needed to raise BAC.,b:If two people are the same weight, the person with more body fat shows intoxication first.,c:Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you the same as drinking three drinks over three hours.
note: Alcohol affects you more when you drink it quickly. Three drinks in one hour will raise your BAC and impair you more than the same three drinks spread over three hours, because your body has less time to process the alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, to whom should you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:On your left.,b:Who arrived before you.,c:Across from your vehicle.
note: At a four‑way stop, drivers proceed in the order they arrive. You must yield to any vehicle that reached the intersection before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must immediately pull as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. You must wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning devices stop before crossing, even if you think you do not see a train.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop and leave a written note with your name, address, and contact information securely attached to the vehicle, then promptly report the collision as required by local law.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they lift.,c:Slow down and drive around the gates.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop at a safe distance behind the gates and wait. Do not drive around or under the gates. Proceed only after the gates are fully raised and you have checked that the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Improve traffic flow.,b:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly below the normal speed of traffic can impede traffic and may result in a citation.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning on wet pavement, you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Slow down.,c:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on a thin layer of water, causing a loss of steering and braking control. The best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning is to slow down when roads are wet, especially during heavy rain or when water is pooling. Avoid sudden moves and keep your tires properly inflated and with good tread.

question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance areas typically have:
options: a:An orange background with black writing.,b:A red background with green writing.,c:A yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary work zone and construction signs in the United States are typically orange with black letters or symbols. The orange color warns drivers that there are changing or unusual conditions ahead, such as lane shifts, workers on or near the roadway, or equipment entering and exiting the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is an important step before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Always move to the left lane.
note: Before making any turn, you must check traffic in all directions: ahead, behind, and to both sides. This helps you judge gaps, see pedestrians, bicyclists, and oncoming vehicles, and decide if it is safe to turn. You should also signal and adjust your speed as needed, but you never speed up just to turn or change lanes without checking traffic.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: After a minor collision with no injuries, if the vehicles are drivable and it is safe, you should move them out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional crashes, keeps traffic moving, and makes it safer for everyone involved. Then exchange information and follow any reporting requirements in your state.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Ease up on the gas pedal.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, gently ease off the accelerator (and the brakes if you were braking) so the tires can regain traction. Sudden braking or turning can make the skid worse. As you ease off the gas, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go until you regain control.

question: If the road is slippery, your following distance should be:
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Closer to the car ahead than normal.,c:Farther from the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads, it takes much longer to stop, so you must increase your following distance. Leave a larger space cushion between you and the vehicle ahead so you have more time and distance to brake gently and avoid skids or rear-end collisions.

question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, you're least likely to have an accident if you:
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Stay within that speed range.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.
note: You are safest when you travel at the same general speed as surrounding traffic, as long as it is within the posted speed limit. Large speed differences—either faster or slower—make lane changes and passing more frequent and increase the chance of conflicts and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a designated left-turn lane with oncoming traffic, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Stay centered in the left‑turn lane with your wheels straight until it is safe to turn.
note: Before making a left turn from a designated left‑turn lane, signal at least 100 feet before the intersection so other drivers know your intentions. Keep your front wheels pointed straight while waiting to turn; if your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Speed up.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Challenge them.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, do not engage with them. Safely move out of their way, allow them to pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures. Creating distance reduces the chance of a confrontation or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.,c:Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution and do not speed up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the driving lane?
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle:
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: You must not drive onto or along the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Passing on the shoulder is unsafe and illegal in normal situations because the shoulder is reserved for emergencies and stopped vehicles.

question: Which of the following will reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not make you sober faster or reduce BAC.

question: You should not use your horn:
options: a:Near blind pedestrians.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.
note: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. They rely on sound cues to navigate, and an unnecessary horn blast can startle or disorient them. Instead, slow down, yield, and give them plenty of space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Driving off the paved roadway or onto the shoulder to pass is unsafe and illegal in most situations. You must stay on the main-traveled, paved portion of the road when passing; if you cannot safely pass within the lane(s) provided, you must wait until it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully for other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe. You are not required to stop, but you must use extra caution because cross traffic may not be fully controlled.

question: Before driving you should remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Before driving, you should clear snow, frost, and ice from all windows and mirrors so you have an unobstructed view in every direction. Good visibility is essential for spotting other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards early enough to react safely.

question: How do you keep aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, check your mirrors regularly—about every few seconds and before changing lanes, slowing, or stopping. This helps you anticipate vehicles that may be following too closely or approaching quickly so you can adjust your driving safely.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross this line to change lanes when it is safe and legal, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: Which of these is true about alcohol and driving?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,b:Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.,c:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.
note: Alcohol affects judgment, decision‑making, reaction time, and coordination, even at low blood alcohol levels. You can feel “okay” or be able to walk straight and still be too impaired to drive safely. The only safe choice after drinking is not to drive.

question: Which roadway surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:A bridge,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because cold air circulates both above and below the surface, causing them to lose heat faster than regular roadways. Even when the main road looks just wet, a bridge can be icy and very slippery.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:All of the above.,c:Alertness and concentration.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, and harm alertness and concentration. Because they affect all of these critical skills, any of the listed abilities can be impaired, so the correct choice is that all are affected.

question: The term "No zones" around large trucks refers to areas where cars:
options: a:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,b:Disappear into blind spots or are so close they limit the truck driver's ability to stop or maneuver safely.,c:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: “No zones” are the large blind spots and danger areas around trucks where the truck driver cannot see you or cannot safely stop or maneuver if you are too close. Avoid lingering beside a truck, cutting in too closely in front, or following too closely behind.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is reduced, you should turn:
options: a:On your parking lights.,b:On your headlights.,c:Up the instrument panel lights.
note: When visibility is reduced by dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, you must turn on your headlights so others can see you more easily. Use low‑beam headlights; parking lights alone are not enough and are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not working, a driver should:
options: a:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,b:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out (no lights showing), you must treat the intersection like an all-way stop. Come to a full stop at the limit line or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is your turn and it is safe, yielding the right‑of‑way as you would at a four‑way stop.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow for turning indicate?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before it changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from that lane.,c:Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow turn arrow means the protected turning phase is ending. You should prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely, you may complete the turn after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Do not speed up to beat the light.

question: When the centerline is a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and prohibited for traffic on the side with the solid line. Drivers on the broken-line side may pass when it is safe and legal; drivers on the solid-line side must not cross to pass.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you while driving in a city, you should:
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Both of the above.
note: Interstate driving involves higher speeds and heavier, faster‑moving traffic. You must be able to control your vehicle safely at these speeds and remain constantly alert to changing traffic, merging vehicles, and road conditions to react in time and avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is:
options: a:65 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: On Tennessee primary and secondary state and federal highways, the default speed limit is 55 mph unless a different limit is posted. Always follow the posted sign if it differs from the general rule.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness and slow your reactions, and they also affect coordination, making it harder to steer, brake, and control the vehicle. Because both alertness and coordination are impaired, any use can make driving unsafe.

question: Construction zone signs are typically:
options: a:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,b:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Work zone and construction signs are usually diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black symbols or wording. The orange color alerts drivers to temporary conditions such as road work, lane shifts, or workers on or near the roadway.

question: How can any amount of alcohol in the blood affect a driver?
options: a:Knowledge.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Right-of-way privileges.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect judgment, making you more likely to take risks, and can reduce physical coordination, making it harder to steer, brake, and react in time. Because of this, driving may be unsafe at any blood alcohol level.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: When passing, move into the passing lane, accelerate to pass the other vehicle safely and promptly, and return to your lane only when you can see the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. Lingering beside another vehicle increases the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, you should:
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.
note: When exiting a driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk or sidewalk area. After stopping, you must yield to any pedestrians on the sidewalk and to traffic in the street before you enter the roadway.

question: How many times more likely are you to cause an accident if your BAC is 0.10% than if you are sober?
options: a:Five,b:Seven,c:Three
note: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) around 0.10% greatly increases crash risk; studies commonly show a driver is about seven times more likely to be involved in a crash than when sober. Any amount of alcohol can impair judgment and reaction time, so you should never drive after drinking.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads you should:
options: a:It is safe to use your cruise control.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, you should slow down and make all speed and steering changes gradually to avoid skids. Sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering can cause loss of control. You should also avoid using cruise control on slippery roads so you can respond quickly to changing traction.

question: Which is true about large trucks compared with passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,b:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need more distance and time to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed. Because of this, you should not cut in front of trucks and should allow extra following distance when driving behind them.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the road ahead, what is the safest action to take?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.,b:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
note: If heavy smoke covers the road and you cannot see clearly, you should slow down, move as far to the right as you safely can, and stop completely off the roadway if possible. Stay stopped with your lights on until visibility improves, rather than continuing to drive into the smoke.

question: Where should a driver direct their attention while driving?
options: a:Stare directly in front of their car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and behind using mirrors and quick glances. This wider awareness helps you spot hazards early, adjust speed or position, and avoid sudden emergencies.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign indicates:
options: a:Warning.,b:Stop.,c:Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or work zones so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver you should:
options: a:Relax and concentrate on driving.,b:Tailgate the driver in front of you.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit.
note: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm, allow extra travel time, and focus on safe driving rather than rushing or competing with other drivers. Avoid tailgating, speeding, or reacting angrily to others’ mistakes.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and safe.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind and along both sides. Even with properly adjusted mirrors, every vehicle has areas you cannot see, so you must turn your head and check over your shoulder when changing lanes.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,b:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, move completely onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your hazard flashers so others see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt on while you call for help. Standing outside near high‑speed traffic is very dangerous.

question: On seeing orange construction signs and cones on a freeway you should:
options: a:Change lanes only if needed and adjust your speed for the work zone.,b:Slow down only if you see a lane ending.,c:Slow down, follow posted work-zone signs, and be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: Orange signs and cones mean a work zone. You should slow down, be prepared to stop, and watch carefully for workers, equipment, lane shifts, and reduced speed limits. Never assume you can maintain your current speed through a construction area.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:Only if a crossing guard is present.,c:At all times.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and has the right‑of‑way at all times. You must stop or yield as needed, never honk at or rush them, and wait until they are safely out of your path before proceeding.

question: When a stopped school bus ahead is loading or unloading children with lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass only if the bus is in a separate roadway where stopping is not required.,b:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus, then proceed only if the red lights are off and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, following any state-specific divided-highway exceptions.
note: When a school bus has red flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Children may cross unexpectedly, so do not move until the bus signals that it is safe by turning off the red lights and pulling in the stop arm.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Before you get into the car.,c:Whenever you need to use them.
note: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors before you start driving so you have a clear view of traffic around you as soon as the vehicle moves. Properly set mirrors reduce blind spots and help you change lanes and turn more safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must obey instructions given by:
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Flaggers (signal persons) in construction or work zones are legally authorized to direct traffic, and their instructions must be obeyed, even if they differ from traffic signals or signs. Security guards in parking lots and other drivers with broken-down vehicles are not generally empowered to control traffic on public roads.

question: What effect can strong wind gusts on highways have?
options: a:They generally affect only large vehicles.,b:They only reduce visibility.,c:They can create problems for all vehicles.
note: Strong wind gusts can push or sway any vehicle, not just large trucks or buses, especially at highway speeds or on open bridges and overpasses. They may also blow debris and dust, reducing visibility. All drivers should reduce speed and maintain a firm grip on the steering wheel in high winds.

question: What do yellow center lines on a road indicate?
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. A single or double solid yellow line means no passing where the solid line is on your side; broken yellow lines allow passing when it is safe. White lines, not yellow, separate traffic moving in the same direction and mark carpool lanes.

question: When is a driver's reaction time likely to be reduced?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain and nervous system, which increases the time it takes to see a hazard, decide what to do, and move your foot to the brake. This longer reaction time greatly increases the chance of a collision, even at low blood alcohol levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you encounter a flashing yellow light at an intersection, do this:
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You must slow down, be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection, and continue only when it is safe. Unlike a flashing red light, you are not required to come to a complete stop unless needed for safety.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should you be especially aware of?
options: a:Watch for multiple trains.,b:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings (school buses, hazardous-material trucks),c:Both of the above.
note: At railroad crossings you must be alert for more than just a single train. A second train can come on another track, and some vehicles—like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials—are required by law to stop at all crossings. Expect these stops and be prepared to slow or stop safely.

question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:
options: a:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,b:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,c:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.
note: When passing parked cars, leave space and be ready for doors to open, people to step out, or vehicles to pull away from the curb. Expect sudden movements into your lane and adjust your speed and position so you can stop or steer around hazards in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What action should you take when you approach a steady yellow light and haven't entered the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you are expected to stop if you can do so safely. Only continue through if stopping would be unsafe, such as if someone is following too closely behind you.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain, you should:
options: a:Put your cruise control on to maintain a constant speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to reduce this risk is to slow down, especially in heavy rain or standing water, and make smooth steering and braking inputs so your tires can grip the pavement.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide. This keeps you in your lane while reducing glare. Avoid looking directly at the headlights, and keep your own low beams on so others can see you.

question: When you are taking any medication, what precaution should you take regarding driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.,c:Have someone follow you home.
note: Prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slower reaction time. Before driving, you should ask your doctor or pharmacist whether the medication can affect your ability to drive safely and follow their advice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red arrow pointing right means you may:
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A steady red arrow means you must not turn in the direction of the arrow. You must stop and wait until a green light or green arrow appears before making the turn.

question: At what BAC can a driver under 21 have their license suspended in Tennessee?
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any detectable amount.
note: For drivers under 21 in Tennessee, any detectable amount of alcohol in the body can result in license suspension. This is called a zero‑tolerance law and is stricter than the 0.08% limit that applies to most drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Require pedestrians to wait for you to cross.
note: Yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection; drivers must yield to pedestrians when turning on a steady green.

question: When should you add extra following distance to the vehicle in front?
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: When another driver is following too closely, increase your following distance from the vehicle ahead. The extra space gives you more time to slow down gradually, reducing the chance that the tailgater will hit you if you must brake.

question: Driving at night is more dangerous mainly because:
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Low light and glare from headlights reduce how much of the road, hazards, and signs you can see, so you must use your headlights properly, reduce speed, and be extra alert.

question: A flashing yellow signal at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution, not stop and not wait for green. Look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and continue only when it is safe.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane you must:
options: a:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.,b:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,c:You must yield the right-of-way.
note: When a pedestrian is using a white cane or a guide dog, they are visually impaired and have the right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed, avoid honking, and allow them to cross safely before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you confirm before merging back after passing?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: After passing another vehicle, only move back into your original lane when you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to merge back without cutting the other driver off.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility you should:
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: When weather reduces visibility, you should slow down and increase your following distance. More space gives you extra time to see hazards and stop smoothly if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

question: Which behavior may indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:The number of passengers in the car.,c:The driver tends to drive slowly.
note: Erratic, unsafe lane changes are a classic sign of aggressive driving. Drivers who weave through traffic, change lanes without signaling, or cut others off are more likely to cause crashes. The number of passengers or simply driving slowly does not, by itself, indicate aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Slow down if needed to safely merge or adjust to traffic.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, signal, and then move only when it is safe. The inside rearview mirror alone is not enough because it does not show vehicles in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Even with a green light, you must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. Entering when traffic is stopped ahead can leave you blocking the intersection when the light changes, which is illegal in many states and dangerous for cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights you must:
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,b:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,c:Stop immediately, even if you are within an intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using siren and flashing lights, you must pull as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in the middle of an intersection; instead, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop until the vehicle has passed.

question: What should you do when an oncoming car's headlights are blinding you at night?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: At night, if oncoming headlights blind you, avoid looking directly at them. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane while the other vehicle passes.

question: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,b:You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.,c:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
note: You must never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. If traffic is stopped ahead and you would have to stop on the tracks, wait behind the stop line until you can cross completely. Being trapped on the tracks is extremely dangerous.

question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:
options: a:Open a window.,b:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine.
note: If you become drowsy, stop at a safe place to rest or switch drivers; short fixes like caffeine are not substitutes for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver should use the proper turn signal how far before beginning a turn?
options: a:100 feet,b:75 feet,c:25 feet
note: Activate your turn signal at least 50 feet before the turn to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow centerlines on streets and highways?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and show that passing is allowed when it is safe and the line on your side is broken. Always check for oncoming traffic and enough clear distance before crossing the centerline to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.,b:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,c:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, hazards can come from the sides, not just straight ahead. Always scan left and right for pedestrians, cyclists, trains, and cross traffic before you proceed, even if you have the right of way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a pedestrian is in the crosswalk when your light turns green, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian in the intersection; wait until they have crossed before you proceed even if your light turns green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you position your vehicle when preparing to turn left from a two-way street?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline.,c:To the right of the centerline but still in your lane.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, you should approach the turn close to the centerline of the road, not the right edge. This position gives you a better turning angle, keeps you out of the path of right‑turning traffic, and lines you up to turn into the proper lane.

question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even one drink may impair your driving ability, so the safest choice is not to drive after consuming any alcohol.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and steer in the direction you want to go.,b:Brake lightly while turning the steering wheel fully.,c:Brake abruptly to stop the skid as quickly as possible.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and stay off the brakes; braking can make the skid worse. Look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, and once you regain traction, slow down gradually. (If your vehicle has ABS and you must brake to avoid a collision, apply firm, steady pressure while continuing to steer.)

question: What must drivers do at a crosswalk?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to you.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked. You must slow or stop to allow pedestrians to cross safely, unless a traffic signal or crossing guard clearly directs the pedestrian to yield.

question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.
note: Emotional upset can impair judgment; give yourself time to calm down before operating a vehicle.

question: Why is driving at night more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to judge distances and speeds. You can only see as far as your headlights illuminate.

question: What should you do as you near the crest of a hill?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: You cannot see what is over the top of a hill; slow and be prepared to stop if there is a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way — so if the other driver is to your left, you go first.

question: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:A good idea if the weather is bad.,c:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can create unsafe passing attempts and increase crash risk; drive with the flow when safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic and pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, and then proceed only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often:
options: a:Does not increase the chance of a crash.,b:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,c:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and often leads to risky choices like late braking, unsafe passing, or running lights. Excessive speed increases both crash likelihood and crash severity.

question: When should you begin slowing for an interstate exit?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: On an interstate, stay at highway speed until you are in the deceleration lane, then begin slowing to the posted ramp or advisory speed. Slowing early on the main roadway can surprise faster traffic and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: Increase your following distance behind a large vehicle primarily to:
options: a:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.,b:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,c:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead. Leaving extra following distance lets you see around them sooner, spot hazards earlier, and gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which should you not do?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened, press your head firmly against the head restraint, and brace yourself. The belt and head restraint help reduce injury and keep you in position to maintain some control of the vehicle.

question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: In construction zones, conditions can change quickly due to workers, equipment, lane shifts, and debris. You should slow down, stay alert, and be ready for sudden stops or changes in traffic patterns. Never assume workers will yield to you; drivers must use extra caution and be prepared for the unexpected.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,b:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They alert inattentive drivers that their vehicles have left the travel lane through vibration and sound.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that cause noise and vibration when you drive over them. This alerts drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or work zone, so they can correct their path in time.

question: What does a steady yellow left-turn arrow tell drivers?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left-turn period is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A steady yellow left‑turn arrow means the protected left‑turn phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so, and you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when the signal changes. It warns that you will no longer have an exclusive right‑of‑way to turn.

question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, use your headlights because:
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, headlights make your vehicle easier for others to see, even during the day. Many states require you to use low‑beam headlights whenever your windshield wipers are on or visibility is reduced. Using headlights in poor weather is about being seen by others, not about improving engine performance.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Maintain a steady speed.,c:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early helps the driver behind you judge distance and react smoothly. Sudden braking or frequent speed changes can cause the following driver to get too close or need to brake hard. Consistent driving gives everyone more time and space to stay at a safe following distance.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Following a motorcycle too closely is dangerous because motorcycles are lighter and can usually stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you are tailgating and the motorcyclist brakes suddenly, you may not have enough time or space to stop, greatly increasing the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How soon before turning must you activate your turn signal?
options: a:At least 50 feet.,b:As soon as you decide to turn.,c:At least 100 feet.
note: You must signal at least 50 feet before the location of your turn to warn other road users of your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should signal continuously when turning because:
options: a:Is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b:It lets other drivers know what your intentions are.,c:Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.
note: You should keep your turn signal on continuously through the turn or lane change so others clearly understand what you are about to do. Signaling the whole time helps nearby drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians predict your path and adjust their speed or position to avoid conflicts.

question: Tennessee law requires children under which age to be secured in an approved child restraint?
options: a:Two,b:Four,c:Three
note: Tennessee law requires that children under age four be secured in an approved child restraint system. Proper child restraints are designed for a child’s size and age and greatly reduce the risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:They expect no breaks and give none.,b:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,c:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, anticipating what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians might do, and being ready to react safely. Instead of assuming others will always follow the rules, a defensive driver leaves space, adjusts speed, and has an escape plan to avoid collisions.

question: When must you use low beam headlights?
options: a:In fog and other low-visibility conditions such as rain, snow, or mist.,b:On a lighted street or when there is oncoming traffic.,c:Both a and b.
note: Use low beam headlights whenever visibility is reduced, such as in fog, rain, snow, or mist, and when driving on lighted city streets or when there is oncoming traffic. High beams can reflect off moisture or fog and can also blind other drivers, so low beams are safer in these conditions.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Try to fight it.,b:Take some caffeine pills.,c:Take a break.
note: If you become drowsy while driving, you must get off the road and rest. Drowsiness greatly slows your reaction time and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Caffeine or trying to fight sleep are not safe substitutes for stopping to rest or changing drivers.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the right.,b:Passing is permitted from the left.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions mean no passing from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: What is the law regarding open alcoholic containers in a vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Illegal in most states for drivers or passengers to drink from or possess open alcoholic containers in a vehicle on a public road.,b:Legal for passengers to drink as long as the driver is sober.,c:Legal for the driver to drink as long as they are not over the legal BAC limit.
note: It is illegal for drivers and passengers to possess or consume open alcoholic beverages in a motor vehicle while on a highway.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough or cold medicines that contain codeine or antihistamines. These drugs can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, and affect judgment, so you should always read labels and avoid driving if a medication can cause drowsiness or impairment.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what should you do?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes.,b:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Use the brakes lightly only after you have the vehicle under control and its speed has dropped. Heavy or sudden braking can cause loss of control, especially with a blown tire.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver should generally:
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: You can never rely on other drivers to follow right‑of‑way rules. Even when you are legally entitled to go first, you should be ready to slow, stop, or yield if it will prevent a collision. Defensive drivers expect mistakes from others and adjust to avoid crashes.

question: What penalties apply to driving under the influence of drugs compared with alcohol?
options: a:A lesser penalty than driving under the influence of alcohol.,b:The same penalty as driving under the influence of alcohol.,c:Absolutely no penalty at all.
note: Driving while impaired by drugs is treated like driving while impaired by alcohol. If a drug—illegal, prescription, or over‑the‑counter—affects your ability to drive safely, you can face the same types of DUI penalties as for alcohol, including fines, license suspension, and possible jail time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b:All approaching vehicles and any pedestrians or bicyclists crossing your path.,c:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing your path.
