You do not have to yield to oncoming vehicles that are also turning left if you both have the same signal and can turn safely, but you must still proceed with caution and be ready to yield if needed to avoid a collision.

question: If cars are approaching on your left and parked cars are on your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: When there are hazards on both sides—oncoming traffic to the left and parked cars to the right—steer a middle course. This keeps you as far as practical from both dangers and gives you more room to react if a door opens or an oncoming vehicle drifts toward the center.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.,b:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,c:Check traffic behind and to the side, then judge the gap ahead before merging.
note: When entering a gap in highway traffic, you must check traffic behind and to the side to be sure it is safe to accelerate, then focus on the gap and vehicles ahead as you merge. Do not rely on other drivers to move for you, and do not watch only one direction; use mirrors and a quick head check, then adjust your speed smoothly to fit into the gap.

question: If you are already in an intersection when the light changes from green to steady yellow you should:
options: a:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.,b:Stop.,c:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. A steady yellow warns that the light is about to turn red; it is not a signal to stop in the middle of the intersection. You should not speed up aggressively, but you should complete your movement and get out of the intersection.

question: You approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended. What must you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. In many states this applies to traffic in both directions on undivided roads. Only proceed once the bus signals that loading or unloading is complete and it is safe to move.

question: If you are the operator involved in a reportable crash, within how many days must you file a report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security?
options: a:48 hours.,b:20 days.,c:10 days.
note: In Tennessee, if you are an operator or owner involved in a reportable crash, you must file the required crash report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security within 20 days. Failing to report within the required time can lead to penalties or license consequences.

question: What is a likely effect at a BAC of 0.02%?
options: a:Won't have any effect on your driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Will double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol in your system can affect judgment, attention, and reaction time. At about 0.02% BAC, your risk of being in a crash is already significantly higher—roughly double compared with a 0.00% BAC—so it is not safe to assume there is no effect or no risk to others.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean vehicles in both directions must stay in their lane and may not cross the lines to pass. You can still cross them only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road where it is otherwise safe and legal, but not for overtaking another vehicle.

question: If you must park in a nonstandard parking area, you should:
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: When you must park where vehicles do not normally park, the key safety rule is to make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions. Use legal parking positions, turn on hazard lights if appropriate, and avoid curves, hills, or obstructions that hide your vehicle from approaching traffic.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Make abrupt turns.
note: On wet roads, tires have less grip and can hydroplane. Slowing down is the most important way to reduce this risk. Combine lower speed with smooth steering, gentle braking, and avoiding sudden moves to help maintain traction.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see vehicles ahead.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.
note: At night on dimly lit streets, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This ensures you have time to react to hazards that appear in your headlight beam. Use low or high beams as appropriate, but always adjust speed to your visible stopping distance.

question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the side mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using the inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle is in that blind spot, then change lanes only if it is clear and safe.

question: What does a curb painted red mean?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there for any reason (except when required by traffic controls or emergency vehicles). It is used where stopping would create a serious hazard, such as near fire hydrants or in front of fire station driveways.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, point your front wheels:
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic.

question: Double solid yellow center lines mean:
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:Neither lane may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean passing is not allowed from either side. You must stay in your lane and may only cross when turning left at an intersection or into a driveway where it is permitted.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Slam on the brakes.,b:Not drive through the flooded area; turn around and find another route.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: If the road ahead is flooded, turn around and find another route. Even shallow water can hide deep holes, debris, or a washed-out road, and moving water can quickly sweep a vehicle away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Always stop before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, and enter when there is a safe gap. Do not stop on the ramp unless traffic or signals require it, and never try to cross multiple lanes at once.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane highways, you should generally travel in the right lane unless passing. If you notice vehicles passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane, it means you are moving slower than the flow of traffic. To drive safely and predictably, you should move to the right lane so faster traffic can pass on the left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The light is about to turn green.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:The same thing as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards, then proceed only when it is safe and your way is clear.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Being late for an appointment.,b:Missing an exit.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Driving while fatigued slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and can cause you to briefly nod off or fall asleep completely. This greatly increases the chance of losing control of the vehicle and being involved in a serious crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic signal turns red while you are in the intersection waiting to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light changes to green.,b:Back out of the intersection, if possible.,c:Complete the turn when traffic clears.
note: If you have already entered the intersection to turn left and the light turns red, you should not back up or stop in the middle of the intersection. Instead, wait until oncoming traffic and pedestrians have cleared, then complete your turn as soon as it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to use extra caution. You do not need to stop, but you must slow down, scan carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: While driving on the highway, consistently looking far ahead helps you:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Allow you to spot upcoming police officers.,c:Help you keep up with traffic.
note: Looking well ahead on the highway lets you see slowing traffic, lane closures, and other hazards early. This extra time means you can ease off the gas or change lanes smoothly instead of braking or turning suddenly, which reduces the risk of rear-end collisions and loss of control.

question: In Tennessee, a DUI conviction is based on which blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:50 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and over in Tennessee, a BAC of 0.08% or higher is considered legally impaired for DUI. Even lower BAC levels can still be dangerous, and drivers under 21 are subject to stricter limits and penalties at much lower BACs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be driving?
options: a:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,b:At the legal speed limit.,c:More slowly than the freeway traffic.
note: Use the on‑ramp to accelerate so you are at or near the speed of freeway traffic when you reach the merging area. Matching the flow of traffic (without exceeding the speed limit) makes it easier and safer to find a gap and merge smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Into which lane should you turn when making a left from a two-way onto a one-way street?
options: a:Turn into any lane.,b:Turn into the first lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning left from a two‑way street onto a one‑way street, start from the lane closest to the centerline and turn into the first lane available on the one‑way street. This keeps your turn tight and predictable and leaves other lanes open for through traffic or other turning vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, you should:
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.,b:Always maintain your position.,c:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
note: Although freeway traffic usually has the right‑of‑way, safe driving means helping merging vehicles when you can. If possible, adjust your speed or change lanes to create a gap so merging drivers can enter smoothly, reducing sudden braking and potential collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is faster behind you in the left lane, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane so you don't impede traffic.,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.
note: On multilane roads, the left lane is generally for passing. If vehicles behind you are moving faster, you should safely move to the right lane when possible so faster traffic can pass. Staying in the left lane when you are slower than traffic can create congestion and increase the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: Which statement about pedal use is correct?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,c:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.
note: Drivers should use the right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This reduces the chance of pressing both pedals at once or hitting the wrong pedal, and it gives you better, more consistent control of the vehicle. Braking should be smooth and controlled, not abrupt, except in emergencies.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers stopped behind must remain stopped until:
options: a:All students are off the bus.,b:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,c:The stop arm is retracted.
note: Do not pass a stopped school bus until its red lights are off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and it begins moving again.

question: In a vehicle with airbags the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride is:
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: In vehicles with airbags, children age 12 and under are safest in the back seat. Front airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure smaller passengers. Children should ride properly restrained in the back seat, using appropriate car seats or booster seats as required by their age, height, and weight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action if another vehicle passes you in a no-passing zone?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down to let the passing vehicle return to the drive lane.
note: If another vehicle begins passing you in a no-passing zone, do not speed up or try to block them. Instead, slightly reduce your speed if needed so the passing driver can return to the lane safely and quickly. This helps prevent head-on collisions and reduces the danger created by their unsafe maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle it is safe to return to your lane when you:
options: a:Have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: On a two-lane road, after you pass another vehicle you should not move back into your lane until you can see the front of the vehicle (its headlights) clearly in your inside rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space ahead of the other vehicle so you can return without cutting them off or forcing them to brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Left, toward the center of the road.,b:Straight ahead.,c:Right, toward the side of the road.
note: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, turn the front wheels to the right, toward the side of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

question: Having a driver's license is a:
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: In the United States, driving is considered a privilege, not a right. The state grants you a license if you meet the requirements, and it can suspend or revoke that license if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing the street (jaywalking), you:
options: a:Should honk your horn at them.,b:Do not have to stop for them.,c:Must stop for them.
note: You must always do what is necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if they are crossing illegally. If pedestrians are in the roadway, slow down and stop if needed so you do not strike them, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs typically?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations you must obey, such as speed limits or no parking zones. They are typically white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

question: The two-second rule is intended to be used when driving at:
options: a:Speeds up to 55 mph.,b:Any speed.,c:Speeds up to 30 mph.
note: The two‑second rule is a general minimum following‑distance guideline at any speed in good conditions. Pick a fixed object ahead; when the vehicle in front passes it, you should pass it at least two seconds later. In bad weather, at night, or with poor visibility, increase this to at least four seconds or more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start your turn from:
options: a:The lane in the center of the road.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:Any lane (as long as it is safe).
note: On a one‑way street, a left turn must start from the lane closest to the left curb, unless signs or lane markings say otherwise. This positions you correctly to turn into the leftmost lane of the new one‑way street and avoids cutting across other lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway you should be driving:
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic already on the freeway, then merge when there is a safe gap. Being much slower than traffic is dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: When encountering slippery surfaces such as ice or snow you should:
options: a:Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.,b:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,c:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
note: On ice or snow, you should slow down, increase following distance, and avoid sudden braking or steering. Before going down a steep hill, shift to a lower gear so the engine helps control your speed and reduces the chance of skidding from heavy brake use.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery during rain?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:If it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining several hours.
note: Pavement is most slippery just after rain begins. Oil, grease, and dust that have built up on the road mix with the first water to form a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this washes away and traction usually improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab.,b:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.,c:Directly behind the body.
note: Large trucks have several large blind spots, often called "no-zones": directly behind the truck, along both sides (especially the right side), and a smaller area directly in front of the cab. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you. Avoid lingering in these areas and give trucks extra space when passing or following.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make constant visual checks.,c:Slow down when driving.
note: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots, you must make frequent visual checks. Scan the road ahead, use your mirrors often, and always check over your shoulder before changing lanes or turning. Never share a lane with a motorcycle; they need a full lane just like any other vehicle.

question: As vehicle speed increases, how are stopping distance and crash severity affected?
options: a:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,b:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,c:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both your stopping distance and the severity of a crash increase. You travel farther before you react, and your vehicle needs more distance to come to a complete stop. In a collision, higher speed means more force on impact, which greatly increases the risk of serious injury or death.

question: What color are traffic control devices used in work zones?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: Traffic control devices in work zones are orange to alert drivers that there are road workers, lane shifts, or other temporary changes ahead. Orange signs, cones, drums, and barriers signal that you should slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for sudden stops or workers and equipment near the roadway.

question: The best action if you become tired while driving is to:
options: a:Open a window.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Stop to rest or change drivers.
note: If you become tired while driving, the safest choice is to stop in a safe place and rest or change drivers. Opening a window or drinking coffee may make you feel briefly more alert, but they do not prevent drowsiness or microsleep. Only rest or sleep can restore your alertness enough to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you not assume when preparing to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.,b:Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.,c:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.
note: When preparing to pass, you must never assume other drivers will create space for you to return to your lane. You are responsible for making sure there is enough clear distance ahead and enough room to move back safely without relying on the other driver to slow down or move over.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration increases, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More coordinated.,c:More sober.
note: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become more impaired. Even small increases in BAC reduce judgment, slow reaction time, and affect coordination, making driving increasingly dangerous.

question: When weather or light conditions require lights, you should use:
options: a:Use your low beams.,b:Use your parking lights only.,c:Use your high beams whenever visibility is reduced.
note: When weather or darkness requires you to turn on your lights, you should use your low-beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle visible to others without causing glare. High beams can reflect off fog, rain, or snow and actually reduce your ability to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn as you pass.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, you must first judge the distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles to be sure you have enough clear space to pass safely. If there is any doubt about whether you can complete the pass before oncoming traffic reaches you, do not start the maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, you should:
options: a:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals. After yielding to the vehicle on your right, proceed when it is your turn and it is safe.

question: How should you steer if the rear of your vehicle skids left?
options: a:Not turn your steering wheel.,b:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, and steer in the same direction the rear is sliding. If the rear skids left, turn the steering wheel left. This helps realign the front of the vehicle with the rear and regain traction and control.

question: If you have consumed three beers within an hour, approximately how long will it take for the alcohol to leave your bloodstream?
options: a:Three hours.,b:One hour.,c:Two hours.
note: A common rule of thumb is that the body processes about one standard drink per hour. After three standard beers consumed in about an hour, it can take roughly three hours for the alcohol to be metabolized. However, impairment can begin with the first drink, and actual elimination time varies by weight, sex, metabolism, and food intake. You should never rely solely on time estimates to decide if you are safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you proceed when a blocked view prevents seeing cross traffic at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and look both ways.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
note: When your view of cross traffic is blocked at an intersection, you must first stop at the appropriate stopping point (limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection). Then inch forward slowly until you can clearly see traffic in both directions. Only proceed when you are sure it is safe. Simply slowing down without stopping can be dangerous when you cannot see cross traffic.

question: When driving in work zones you should:
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: In work zones, traffic can stop or change suddenly, and workers or equipment may enter the lane unexpectedly. You should avoid tailgating and leave extra following distance so you have time to react. Combine this with obeying posted work-zone speed limits and watching carefully for signs, cones, and workers.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what must you avoid doing?
options: a:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route.,b:Proceed to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, you must never back up on the freeway or on the shoulder because traffic is moving at high speeds and drivers do not expect a vehicle reversing. Instead, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a route back to your intended exit.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side, while a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. When the two appear together, only drivers on the side with the broken line may cross the centerline to pass; drivers on the solid-line side must not pass.

question: For quick and controlled turns, where should your hands be on the wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: For best control, place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions. This gives you better leverage, control in emergencies, and keeps your arms away from the airbag deployment path.

question: Emergency crossovers on Tennessee interstates may be used by:
options: a:To turn around when no other vehicles are present.,b:To make a U-turn when you missed your exit.,c:Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.
note: Emergency crossovers on interstates are reserved for authorized vehicles such as police, fire, EMS, and highway maintenance. Regular drivers must not use them to turn around or make U‑turns, even if traffic seems light or they miss an exit.

question: A broken yellow centerline between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed in either direction when it can be done safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should never:
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Lane changes should always be planned and smooth. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, signal, and then move over gradually. Sudden or spontaneous lane changes increase the risk of collisions.

question: How far should your body be from the steering wheel for good posture?
options: a:Six to eight inches.,b:10 to 12 inches.,c:18 to 24 inches.
note: Sitting about 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel helps reduce the risk of injury from the airbag while still allowing you to reach the pedals and wheel comfortably and maintain good control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you perform a lane change?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Lane changes should always be made gradually and carefully: signal in advance, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and move smoothly into the next lane only when there is a safe gap.

question: When parking on any hill you should:
options: a:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park.",c:Your front wheels should be parallel to the road, if there is no curb.
note: On any hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park (or in gear for a manual). Then turn the front wheels appropriately depending on whether there is a curb and which way the vehicle would roll, so the car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,b:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow. You must wait until the arrow turns green or a different signal permits the movement before proceeding in that direction.

question: What is the safest action if you must pass a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle approaches?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.,b:Keep driving at the same speed because the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: When you must pass a pedestrian and there is oncoming traffic, slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. This gives you more space and time so you can move around the pedestrian safely without squeezing between them and the oncoming car.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c:Continue ahead; the motorist has the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and wait until pedestrians have completely crossed your lane before proceeding. Never drive around pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

question: A vehicle is following you too closely on a two-lane road. How should you react?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,b:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.,c:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
note: If someone is following too closely, avoid sudden braking or speeding up. Gradually slow down to increase your following distance ahead and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. If there is a safe opportunity, change lanes or pull over briefly to let them go by.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (usually an insurance card) and show it to law enforcement when you are involved in a collision or when an officer requests it during a traffic stop or citation. Failing to provide proof can result in fines or other penalties.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur when:
options: a:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Crash risk increases when one vehicle’s speed is much faster or slower than surrounding traffic because it creates more passing, lane changes, and conflicts. When safe and legal, travel at a speed close to the flow of traffic, without exceeding the speed limit.

question: When driving through a construction zone you should:
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Pass carefully and avoid 'rubbernecking.',c:Stop to watch the workers.
note: In construction zones, stay focused on the road, obey all signs and flaggers, and maintain a safe following distance. Do not slow down just to look at the work (rubbernecking), and never stop to watch workers unless directed to stop by traffic control.

question: What effect does excessive speed have on crash outcomes?
options: a:Saves time.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed greatly increases both the chance of a crash and the severity of injuries when a crash occurs. The faster you are going, the more distance you need to stop and the more force is involved in a collision, which leads to a higher risk of serious injury or death.

question: When driving in fog you should:
options: a:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
note: In fog, you should slow down and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams and, if equipped, fog lights help you see the road and help others see you without creating glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before you change lanes you should check your mirrors and also:
options: a:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,b:Glance over your shoulder.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where another vehicle may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed so the other driver can judge the pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as that can trap the passing vehicle beside you or cause a collision.

question: If you see a deep puddle ahead, what is the safest action?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: If you see a deep puddle, the safest choice is to avoid it if you can do so safely. Deep water can hide potholes or debris, cause hydroplaning, or damage your vehicle. If you must drive through water, slow down and proceed carefully, but never speed up to push through it.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Allow a larger following distance.,c:Be ready to use your horn.
note: When following a motorcycle, leave more space than you would for a car. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly, and the rider is much more exposed. A 3–4 second following distance gives you time to react if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant. It slows brain and nervous system activity, reducing judgment, reaction time, coordination, and alertness, which makes driving much more dangerous even at low concentrations.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be ready to stop if they are in or near the roadway or if a crossing guard signals you to stop. You do not stop automatically unless a sign, signal, or situation requires it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right while on an interstate, what is usually best?
options: a:Change lanes to the left.,b:Slow down.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: On interstates, traffic often enters from on‑ramps on the right. When it is safe, moving one lane to the left gives merging drivers more room and reduces conflicts. If you cannot safely change lanes, adjust your speed as needed to create a safe gap.

question: How should you respond if an oncoming driver does not dim bright lights?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead at the headlights.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide until the vehicle passes, helping protect your night vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,b:Should slow down but never stop.,c:Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop, giving the right‑of‑way to any cross or merging traffic that is close enough to be a hazard. You only proceed when you are sure you can enter or cross without forcing other drivers to slow or change lanes suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into traffic after parking at a curb, you should:
options: a:Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.
note: When pulling out from a curb, you must signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and wait for a gap large enough to accelerate smoothly up to the speed of traffic. Entering too slowly or forcing others to brake or swerve is unsafe and can cause crashes.

question: Recent studies show the number of alcohol-related fatal crashes in Tennessee has:
options: a:Has increased.,b:Has decreased.,c:Has remained steady.
note: Alcohol‑related fatal crashes have generally decreased over the long term due to enforcement, education, and safer vehicles, but specific state trends can change over time. For the real exam, always rely on the most current official Tennessee Driver License Manual data, as statistics in questions must match the latest published figures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: You may only pass where signs and pavement markings allow it and where you have enough clear distance to do so safely. Passing in intersections or on curves and hills is dangerous because your view of oncoming traffic is limited and other drivers may be turning or entering the roadway.

question: Continuous hard braking on snow or ice often:
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Keeps the brakes from freezing.,c:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.
note: On snow or ice, hard or continuous braking can cause the wheels to lock, especially the front wheels, which makes you lose steering control and can lead to a skid. Instead, slow down early, brake gently, and, if equipped, let ABS work by pressing the pedal firmly and steadily without pumping.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light pattern aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off water droplets in fog, rain, or snow and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Four-way flashers are for breakdowns or emergencies, not for normal driving in fog.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while it flashes.
note: A flashing red light means you must treat the intersection like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe. You do not remain stopped the whole time it flashes, and simply slowing down is not enough.

question: What is a likely consequence of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.
note: Tailgating greatly increases your chance of a rear-end collision because you do not have enough space to react and stop. It is considered aggressive driving, can anger other drivers, and can lead to traffic citations. Following at a safe distance gives you time to react to sudden stops or hazards.

question: Which of the following is true about driving speed?
options: a:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or make sudden lane changes and risky passing maneuvers. Safe driving means choosing a speed that is legal and appropriate for road, traffic, and weather conditions—not too fast and not unreasonably slow.

question: Driving while impaired by medication is permitted:
options: a:If it is prescribed by a physician.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not drive if any medication or drug—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—impairs your ability to drive safely. Even if a doctor prescribed it or you do not feel very drowsy, if the drug affects your judgment, reaction time, or coordination, you are not safe or legal to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your wheels drop off the roadway's edge, you should:
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and avoid sudden steering. Slow down on the shoulder, check for traffic, and only when it is safe, gently steer back onto the roadway. Jerking the wheel or turning sharply can cause you to lose control or skid into oncoming traffic.

question: By law, brakes on every vehicle (other than a motorcycle) must:
options: a:Not lock under any condition.,b:Consist of a good foot brake and an emergency or parking brake.,c:Consist of a good parking brake that is capable of stopping the vehicle within legal limits.
note: Tennessee law requires vehicles to have both a functioning foot brake and an emergency/parking brake.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed from either direction when it is safe. You may cross the line to pass only if you have enough clear distance ahead, no oncoming traffic is close, and passing is not otherwise prohibited by signs or conditions.

question: When you approach a pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn as you proceed past them.,b:Carefully drive around them.,c:Stop until the person is well away from your path.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and has the right-of-way. You must stop and remain stopped until the person has safely crossed and is well clear of your path. Do not honk or try to squeeze around them, as this can confuse or endanger the pedestrian.

question: What are potential legal consequences if you cause a fatal crash while impaired?
options: a:Be charged with vehicular homicide.,b:Be fined and sentenced to prison.,c:Both of the above.
note: If you cause a fatal crash while driving impaired, you can be charged with serious crimes such as vehicular homicide or similar offenses. Conviction can bring heavy fines, a long prison sentence, and license revocation, in addition to a permanent criminal record.

question: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, what is the first action to take?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: If another vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, ease off the accelerator first to create more following distance without making a sudden move that could cause skidding or a rear-end collision from a driver behind you. After lifting off the gas, be ready to brake smoothly and adjust your lane position if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is unlawful to:
options: a:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,c:Both of the above.
note: You may not pass in any marked no-passing zone or at a railroad crossing. These areas are designated no-passing because sight distance is limited or the location is inherently hazardous. Always stay in your lane and wait until you are past the crossing or out of the no-passing zone before attempting to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill, what should you do with your front wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn the front wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the front tire will roll into the curb or edge and help stop the vehicle instead of letting it roll into traffic.

question: How many points on your driving record in 12 months will trigger an advisory letter for adults?
options: a:Varies by state; check your DMV handbook.,b:Six points in 12 months in all states.,c:Eleven points in 12 months in all states.
note: In many states, including California, adult drivers receive a warning or advisory letter when they accumulate 2 points in 12 months, 4 points in 24 months, or 6 points in 36 months. The specific “6–11 points in 12 months” threshold is not a standard rule and varies by state, so you must check your own state’s DMV handbook for the exact point levels that trigger advisory letters or other actions.

question: When may you cross double yellow centerlines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When both yellow lines are solid.,b:Whenever traffic ahead is moving under the speed limit.,c:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
note: You may cross double yellow lines to pass only when it is a broken yellow line on your side of the center and it is safe and legal to do so. If there are double solid yellow lines, you must not cross them to pass. The correct condition is that the line next to your lane is broken, not the one on the opposite side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is a left turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street permitted?
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, you may turn left only if traffic on the street you are turning onto also moves to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. This allows you to turn into the left lane of the new one‑way street safely.

question: A large truck turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction:
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Large trucks need more space to turn because their rear wheels track closer to the curb than the front wheels. When turning right, a truck may need to swing wide to the left before completing the turn. You should never try to squeeze by a truck on the right while it is turning.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: When following another vehicle at night, use your low‑beam headlights so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and blind them. High beams are for open road use when there is no vehicle directly ahead of you or approaching you.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.
note: You must always do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or not obeying signals. Yield the right‑of‑way as needed and be prepared to stop, because pedestrians are more vulnerable in any collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when you are turning left at an intersection?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians crossing the street you are turning into. Wait until it is safe and clear before completing your left turn.

question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:
options: a:Driving down long, gradual hills.,b:Driving in long, gradual curves.,c:Driving up long or steep hills.
note: Large trucks are heavy and require a lot of engine power to climb. On long or steep uphill grades, they often cannot maintain speed and will slow down significantly, even with the accelerator fully pressed. Drivers following trucks on hills should be prepared for this speed loss and allow extra space.

question: What is the definition of a crosswalk?
options: a:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross. It can be marked with painted lines or exist legally as an unmarked crosswalk at many intersections. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks.

question: Blue road signs generally provide information about:
options: a:Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Motorist services.
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals. This helps drivers find essential services while traveling.

question: Roads are most slippery:
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Roads are especially slippery just after it starts to rain because water mixes with oil, grease, and other residues on the surface, creating a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and the road usually becomes less slippery, though drivers should always use caution on wet pavement.

question: Which type of road area is most likely to freeze and be slippery after precipitation?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Shaded road areas, such as those under trees or bridges, freeze before open areas and stay frozen longer because they receive less sunlight. Even when the rest of the road looks clear, these shaded spots can still be icy and very slippery, so drivers should slow down and be especially cautious when passing through them.

question: After you change your residence address, how long do you have to notify the Tennessee Department of Safety?
options: a:45 days.,b:10 days.,c:Six months.
note: Tennessee law requires drivers to notify the Department of Safety of a change of residential address within 10 days. This ensures your license and records stay current and that you receive important notices.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road is stopped with red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. This protects children who may be crossing the road.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge distances, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Use high beams only when appropriate and never look directly into oncoming headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do you know you have enough space to return to the driving lane after passing?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: On a freeway you should look farther ahead than on a city street in order to:
options: a:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:See potential hazards early.
note: On a freeway, speeds are higher, so things develop more quickly. Looking farther ahead helps you spot slow traffic, crashes, or debris early so you can adjust smoothly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk. What must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: When a vehicle stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop and not pass it. There may be pedestrians in front of the stopped vehicle that you cannot see. Wait until all pedestrians have completely cleared the crosswalk before proceeding.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway you should:
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Speed up to scare them away.
note: When animals are near the roadway, slow down and be prepared to stop. Animals can move unpredictably into your path, and there may be more animals following. Swerving or speeding up increases the risk of losing control or causing a collision.

question: What can happen if you mix prescription drugs and alcohol and drive?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over‑the‑counter drugs can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment. This combination can make you unfit to drive safely, even if each substance alone might seem mild.

question: Which of these vehicle types is NOT required to stop before crossing any railroad grade crossing in Tennessee?
options: a:Taxis.,b:School or church buses.,c:Farm trucks hauling produce.
note: Vehicles such as school buses and certain buses or trucks carrying passengers or hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings. Ordinary taxis are not in this category and are not required to stop at every crossing unless a traffic control device or law at that specific crossing requires it.

question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or other roadside event, known as rubbernecking, disrupts traffic flow and can cause congestion and additional collisions. Keep your attention on the road and maintain a steady, safe speed instead.

question: Using a cell phone while driving is distracting because it:
options: a:Occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:Causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,c:Is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it can take your hands off the wheel (manual distraction), your eyes off the road (visual distraction), and your mind off driving (cognitive distraction). All three types of distraction greatly increase your risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely on the left side mirror.,b:Rely on the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, signal, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may not appear in your mirrors.

question: When backing up your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Press hard on the gas pedal.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Look directly through the rear window while backing up.
note: When backing up, turn your head and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Mirrors alone do not show everything behind you, and backing too quickly makes it harder to react to people, vehicles, or objects in your path.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle you should:
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your lane. Slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared for unexpected movements instead of assuming they are fully in control.

question: What should you activate if dust or smoke reduces visibility?
options: a:Emergency flashers (with low‑beam headlights).,b:Parking lights only.,c:Headlights only.
note: In heavy dust or smoke where visibility is severely reduced, turn on your low‑beam headlights and your emergency flashers so other drivers can see you from behind and from a distance. Avoid using only parking lights, and slow down or pull off the road if conditions become too dangerous.

question: If you are next to a single broken white line on a highway, what does that mean?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. When you are next to a single broken white line, you may cross it to pass or change lanes, but only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If it seems your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (hydroplaning or loss of traction), the first thing to do is gently ease your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake or turn suddenly; let the vehicle slow down gradually until the tires regain traction.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags:
options: a:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,b:Seat belts should still be worn.,c:Seat belts do not need to be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. You must still wear your lap and shoulder belt properly, even in a vehicle equipped with airbags, for the best protection in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Using your rearview and side mirrors and briefly looking over your shoulder before merging.,b:Using your rearview mirror only.,c:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder but not checking the rearview mirror.
note: When entering a freeway, you should check traffic by using both your rearview and side mirrors and also quickly looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot before merging. Relying only on one mirror or only on a shoulder check is not enough to see all nearby vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a red light?
options: a:If you are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,b:If you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.,c:If you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: In many U.S. states, after coming to a complete stop and if there is no sign prohibiting it, you may turn left on a red light only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street. You must yield to pedestrians and all oncoming traffic before completing the turn.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
note: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots along their sides, especially on the right. Avoid driving next to them for long periods so the driver can see you and you have room to react if the truck needs to change lanes or stop suddenly.

question: Which lights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you.

question: To check for objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Over your left or right shoulder.,b:Only the left outside mirror.,c:Only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, quickly glance over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward to check the blind spot and make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or pedestrian is hidden there.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Large trucks and buses have much bigger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, so it is especially important not to linger alongside them or directly behind them where the driver cannot see you.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will rest against the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights is approaching. What should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,b:Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren while you are already in an intersection, you should not stop in the middle of the intersection. Instead, safely clear the intersection first, then pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: When exiting the freeway on a downhill curved ramp, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: On downhill, curved exit ramps, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while turning, especially downhill, can cause skidding or loss of control, so adjust your speed in advance while traveling straight.

question: When an oncoming car fails to dim its high beams and impairs your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look straight ahead in your lane.,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams at night, avoid looking directly into the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide, checking the other vehicle only from the corner of your eye so your night vision is less affected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle moving in the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting it off.

question: The first driving-related ability that alcohol impairs is:
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making, even before obvious physical skills like balance or clear vision. Impaired judgment leads drivers to take risks, misjudge distances and speeds, and react poorly to hazards, which is why any drinking can make driving unsafe.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning on a wet road?
options: a:You may hydroplane at 45 mph.,b:Hydroplaning can begin at about 35 mph.,c:Hydroplaning occurs only above 40 mph.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as about 35 mph on wet roads, especially where water is standing and tires are worn or underinflated. To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, you should slow down in heavy rain, drive on properly inflated tires with good tread, and avoid puddles and standing water whenever possible.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you turn on to help others see your vehicle?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: When daylight begins to fade, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road more clearly. Parking lights alone are not sufficient for driving, and emergency flashers are only for stopped or emergency situations, not normal driving.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Allow more following distance than you would for a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow at the same distance you would for a passenger vehicle.,c:Follow more closely because motorcycles can stop faster.
note: When following a motorcycle, you should allow more following distance than you would for most other vehicles. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly and are harder to see, so extra space gives you more time to react if the rider slows or swerves suddenly.

question: What is the likely result of continually passing other cars on a two-lane road?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Frequently passing other vehicles on a two-lane road greatly increases your risk of a head-on or side-swipe collision because you must enter the oncoming lane. Safe drivers pass only when it is legal, necessary, and clearly safe, and they avoid constant lane changes and passing maneuvers.

question: When parking next to a curb you should signal:
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
note: You must signal any time you change your vehicle’s direction or position on the road. When parking next to a curb, signal as you move toward the curb so others know you are slowing and moving right, and signal again when pulling away from the curb to re-enter traffic.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Immediately slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
note: When you see a child who looks like they might run into the street, your first response should be to immediately slow down and be ready to stop. Children are unpredictable and may suddenly enter your path. Use your horn only if it will clearly help warn the child without startling them into danger, but always prioritize reducing speed and preparing to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you may legally drive under ideal conditions, not a speed you must always drive. When visibility, traffic, weather, or road conditions are less than ideal, you must drive slower than the posted maximum so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: When must a slow-moving vehicle pull over to let others pass?
options: a:When several vehicles are lined up behind.,b:When five or more vehicles are lined up behind.,c:Only when an emergency vehicle is behind.
note: On many U.S. roads, a slow-moving driver must pull over at the first safe opportunity when five or more vehicles are lined up behind. This prevents traffic backups and reduces risky passing maneuvers. If you notice a long line of vehicles behind you and you are traveling well below the normal flow, use a turnout or safe shoulder area to let them pass.

question: An orange and red triangular sign displayed on a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:Shoulder work ahead.,c:Slow-moving vehicle.
note: An orange and red reflective triangle on the rear of a vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle typically travels 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or some construction vehicles. When you see this sign, slow down, be patient, and pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: If you are not the first person at a crash scene and your help is not needed, you should:
options: a:Stop and look for your own curiosity.,b:Slow down to calm your nerves.,c:Drive on and not interfere with emergency procedures.
note: If you arrive at a crash scene and emergency personnel are already there and managing the situation, you should continue driving and not stop out of curiosity. Unnecessary stopping or slowing can cause additional crashes, block access for emergency vehicles, and distract responders from their work.

question: What must you do when facing a green arrow signal?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield only to pedestrians in the intersection.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you proceed.

question: Parking is illegal in which of the following locations?
options: a:Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,b:Both within 15 feet of a fire hydrant and within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,c:Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
note: Parking is prohibited within a certain distance of key safety areas. You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant so firefighters can access it quickly, and you may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing so trains and warning devices remain clearly visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered on a green light.,b:During rush hour.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You should never enter an intersection unless you are sure you can completely clear it. Even with a green light, if traffic ahead is stopped and you would be left blocking cross traffic, you must wait behind the stop line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should return to your original lane when:
options: a:You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,b:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and reduces the risk of cutting the other driver off.

question: On the freeway behind a large truck, you should follow:
options: a:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,c:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.
note: Large trucks block your view of the road ahead and need more distance to stop. You should follow them at a greater distance than you would a passenger car so you have more time to react and can see traffic conditions ahead.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rain?
options: a:Drive at a speed suitable for ideal conditions.,b:Apply your brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, you should slow down in wet conditions so your tires can maintain better contact with the road. Driving at high speeds on wet pavement causes your tires to ride up on a thin layer of water, reducing steering and braking control.

question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Vehicles.,c:Dangerous.
note: On the road, bicycles are treated as vehicles. Cyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles, including obeying traffic signals, signs, and lane rules.

question: During rainy weather, when should you be most cautious when turning or stopping?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:During the first half hour of rain.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: The road is most slippery during the first part of a rainstorm because oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water before being washed away. During this time, you should be especially cautious when turning or stopping.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down the central nervous system, which impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving unsafe even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.
