note: You must not make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility in these areas makes it difficult to judge oncoming traffic, increasing the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you see a steady yellow light and are not yet in the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must slow down and come to a complete stop before the intersection, rather than speeding up to try to beat the red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:Change lanes without signaling.
note: On interstates, you must always signal before changing lanes so other drivers know your intentions. Slower traffic should keep right, and if you miss your exit you must continue to the next one rather than stopping or backing up. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and illegal.

question: Which statement about medications and driving is correct?
options: a:Most cold and allergy medicines can cause drowsiness.,b:Over-the-counter medicines never affect driving when taken as directed.,c:Medications prescribed by a doctor are always safe to take before driving.
note: Many cold and allergy medicines, even over-the-counter ones, can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Both prescription and nonprescription drugs can impair driving, so always read labels and follow your doctor’s or pharmacist’s advice before driving.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety action should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Before starting the vehicle, you should make it a habit to buckle your own seat belt and check that all passengers are properly buckled. Ensuring everyone is restrained before you drive greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Take your foot off the accelerator, hold the wheel firmly, and brake gently after the vehicle slows.,c:Turn quickly onto the shoulder and stop immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and take your foot off the accelerator to let the car slow down gradually. Avoid braking until the vehicle has slowed, then brake gently as needed and steer to a safe place off the road. Hard or sudden braking can cause loss of control, especially with a front-tire blowout.

question: What should you do if your vehicle starts to skid?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay off the brakes and off the accelerator. Sudden braking can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. Instead, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, and make smooth steering corrections until you regain control.

question: If the rear of your car starts skidding to the left, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Steer to the right.,b:Steer to the left.,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: When the rear of your vehicle skids, you should steer in the same direction that the rear is skidding. If the rear moves left, steer left; if it moves right, steer right. This helps realign the vehicle with your intended path. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, which can cause you to lose further control.

question: Which factor listed affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Body weight is one of the main factors that affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed and how strongly it affects you. In general, a smaller person will reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a larger person after drinking the same amount. Other factors include biological sex, how much food is in the stomach, and how quickly the drinks are consumed, but only time can reduce the alcohol level in the body.

question: Backing up a vehicle is:
options: a:Only dangerous in large vehicles.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Always dangerous.
note: Backing up is always risky because your view to the rear and sides is limited, and it is harder to see small children, pedestrians, or obstacles. Whenever you must back up, move slowly, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, and use a helper or backup camera when available, but still understand that reversing remains a hazardous maneuver.

question: If you park facing uphill with no curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep your wheels facing straight.,b:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: When parking facing uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will move off the roadway instead of into traffic. With a curb, you turn the wheels away from the curb when facing uphill so the tire will roll back against the curb.

question: When driving in fog or mist you should not use high beam headlights because:
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,c:Approaching vehicles might not see you.
note: High beams shine light higher and more intensely. In fog or mist, this light reflects off the water droplets and bounces back into your eyes, creating glare and making it harder to see. Use low beams in fog so the light aims lower at the road and improves visibility.

question: When should you increase your following distance to allow extra space?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a small passenger car.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever you are behind a vehicle whose driver cannot easily see directly behind them, such as large trucks, vans, buses, or vehicles towing trailers. These drivers have larger blind spots and may not see you when they slow, stop, or change lanes, so extra space gives you more time to react and helps avoid collisions.

question: As your speed increases, it becomes more important to:
options: a:Change lanes frequently.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Look well ahead of your vehicle.
note: At higher speeds you cover more distance in less time, so hazards appear and change more quickly. Looking well ahead of your vehicle gives you more time to see problems early, adjust your speed, and change lanes safely if needed.

question: To view vehicles in your blind spots you should check:
options: a:Over your shoulders.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:The inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show the areas directly alongside your vehicle, called blind spots. To check these areas before changing lanes or merging, briefly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move while keeping control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn if it is safe, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection. Proceed at a safe, reasonable speed and be prepared to stop if the light changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:No one.
note: When you turn left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard, whether those vehicles are going straight or making a lawful turn. Overtaking (passing) cars behind you do not have the right-of-way over oncoming traffic when you are turning left.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, you should:
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.,c:Stop in the right lane.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, you should move it as far off the traveled portion of the highway as possible, ideally with all four wheels off the roadway. This reduces the risk of being hit by passing traffic and keeps the lane clear for other drivers.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving you should:
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,c:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: When your vehicle has a mechanical problem, you should signal, carefully move off the road to a safe place, and turn on your hazard lights. Stopping in a traffic lane is very dangerous and should be done only if the vehicle cannot move at all.

question: How should you change your driving when the road is wet or icy?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up.
note: On wet or icy roads, your tires have less grip, so it takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid. You should slow down below the posted speed limit and make all steering, braking, and accelerating movements more gently.

question: What is the legal status of holding a driver's license?
options: a:Right, not a privilege.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Requirement.
note: In the United States, driving is considered a privilege granted by the state, not an automatic right. You must meet licensing requirements, follow traffic laws, and can lose this privilege if you violate those laws.

question: When are you permitted to double park?
options: a:To load or unload passengers.,b:On a four-lane street only.,c:Never.
note: Double parking means stopping or parking beside a vehicle already parked at the curb. This blocks traffic and can hide other vehicles or pedestrians, so it is prohibited. Always pull into a legal parking space or designated loading area instead of stopping alongside parked vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection you should:
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,b:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap and the way is clear before turning, even if you are in the intersection on a green light.

question: Your vehicle's wheels have slipped off the pavement edge. What is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.,b:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the gas, and brake gently to slow down. Once you have control and your speed is reduced, check for traffic and then steer back onto the pavement gradually. Jerking the wheel or braking hard can cause you to lose control or skid into traffic.

question: What penalties apply on a first DUI conviction when the driver has no prior DUI convictions?
options: a:A $100 fine, 24 hours in jail, and a six-month revocation.,b:A $500 fine, 12 hours in jail, and a three-month revocation.,c:A $350 fine, 48 hours in jail, and a one-year revocation.
note: Penalties for a first DUI conviction vary by state, but they typically include a combination of fines, possible jail time, and a license suspension or revocation. Many states set minimum jail times around 24–48 hours and license loss periods from several months up to a year, with higher penalties for very high BAC levels or aggravating factors. Always check your specific state’s DUI laws, but understand that any DUI conviction carries serious legal and financial consequences.

question: If your vehicle has a lap and shoulder belt system, you should:
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: With a lap and shoulder belt system, you must wear both parts. The lap belt should fit low over your hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the middle of your chest and shoulder. Using only one part greatly reduces protection and can cause serious injury in a crash.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the standard term for the amount of alcohol in a person’s blood. It is usually expressed as a percentage, and higher BAC levels mean greater impairment and higher crash risk.

question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Avoid speeding up when approaching curves; enter curves at a safe, steady speed.,b:Slow down before entering curves and intersections so you can steer smoothly.,c:Use lower gears on long, steep downgrades to help control speed, but avoid sudden downshifts that could cause skids on slippery roads.
note: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, slow down before you enter curves and intersections so you can steer smoothly. Sudden acceleration, braking, or sharp steering on a slippery surface can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb, keep the wheels pointed straight ahead.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light, keep the wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway, turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic or into the curb if the brakes fail.
note: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually start turning. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. When parking on hills, you should turn your wheels so the car will roll away from traffic or into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: You should reduce your speed before entering a curve so you can steer smoothly and maintain traction. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause your tires to lose grip and the vehicle to skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Go through the intersection without stopping as directed.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s instructions even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs. If the officer directs you to go through a red light, proceed through the intersection as directed, as long as it is safe to do so.

question: If it is very foggy, slow down and:
options: a:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams (and fog lights if you have them) help you see the road and help others see you.

question: What is true about driving in roadwork zones?
options: a:Fines are often higher and special safety rules apply in work zones.,b:You must Slow for the Cone Zone and obey all posted work zone signs.,c:You should slow only if signs or conditions in the work zone require it.
note: Roadwork zones usually have reduced speed limits and often higher fines for violations. You must slow down, obey all posted signs, and be prepared for workers, equipment, and sudden stops. "Slow for the Cone Zone" reminds drivers to reduce speed and use extra caution whenever they enter a work zone, whether or not workers are visibly present.

question: If the centerline is one solid yellow and one broken yellow and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You are in a passing zone and may pass if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: A centerline with one solid yellow and one broken yellow means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present. The solid line side may not cross to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:
options: a:The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,b:You signal your intention for three seconds.,c:You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After you pass another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the headlights (or front bumper) of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline next to your lane allow?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means you may cross it to pass a vehicle ahead of you on the left, but only when the lane is clear, there is no oncoming traffic, and passing is otherwise safe and legal.

question: When should you use your vehicle's horn?
options: a:Another driver makes a mistake.,b:It may help prevent a collision.,c:Another vehicle is in your way.
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision or warn others of a hazard. Do not use it to show anger, complain about other drivers’ mistakes, or try to force someone to move.

question: How close to the curb must your wheels be when parallel parked?
options: a:Within two feet of the curb.,b:Within 18 inches of the curb.,c:Within one foot of the curb.
note: Many states require your wheels to be within 18 inches of the curb when parallel parked, but some states use different distances (for example, 12 inches). Always check your own state’s driver handbook for the exact legal distance where you live.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,b:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children on bicycles are smaller and harder to see, and they often lack the judgment and reflexes of adults. They may make sudden or unpredictable moves, so give them extra space and slow down, especially near schools, parks, and residential areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, you should adjust your speed so you can merge smoothly into traffic. If there is no gap, ease off the accelerator and be prepared to adjust your speed, but avoid stopping at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, because it makes it hard to accelerate to freeway speed and can be dangerous.

question: A flashing red traffic light indicates you must:
options: a:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,b:May not proceed until it changes to green.,c:Are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel to turn quickly and safely?
options: a:9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions.,b:11 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions.,c:7 o'clock and 5 o'clock positions.
note: For most modern vehicles with airbags, placing your hands at about the 9 o’clock and 3 o’clock positions gives you the best control and leverage for quick, precise steering while keeping your arms out of the main airbag deployment path.

question: What is the only proven way to eliminate alcohol from your system?
options: a:Breathe in some fresh air.,b:Give your body time.,c:Drink coffee.
note: Your body must metabolize alcohol over time; nothing you do—such as drinking coffee, getting fresh air, or exercising—can speed up this process or quickly lower your blood alcohol concentration.

question: Which action demonstrates defensive driving?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.
note: Defensive drivers constantly move their eyes to check ahead, behind, and to the sides so they can spot hazards early and react in time, rather than staring only at the vehicle directly in front of them.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in the right lane as much as possible.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane. When passing, move completely into the left lane before and during the pass so you do not crowd or share the lane with the motorcycle.

question: How should you make room for vehicles merging onto the freeway?
options: a:Slowing down.,b:Merging into a different lane.,c:Maintaining your speed and position.
note: When traffic allows, the safest way to help merging vehicles is to change lanes away from the merge area so they have a clear space to enter. If you cannot safely move over, adjust your speed—either slightly slowing down or speeding up when safe—so there is a safe gap for the merging driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A major contributing factor in fatal traffic crashes in Tennessee is:
options: a:Following too closely.,b:Speeding.,c:Turning into the wrong lane.
note: Speeding is one of the leading contributing factors in severe and fatal crashes. Driving faster than the posted limit or too fast for conditions greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity, making it a major cause of deadly collisions.

question: What is the correct immediate action if a tire blows out?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly without slowing down gradually.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes or use them very lightly, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have control and your speed has dropped, steer carefully to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may pass a vehicle ahead of you by crossing the line, but only when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, so passing is done to the left, never by driving to the right shoulder.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights,b:Low beam headlights,c:High beam headlights
note: In rain, snow, sleet, or fog, use low-beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without causing extra glare.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross where you want to turn right, you should:
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,b:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog has the right-of-way. You must stop and wait until the person has completely crossed the street before you turn. Do not give verbal instructions or try to direct them; simply yield and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which road marking condition are you permitted to pass?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken centerline next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe and legal to do so. A solid line next to your lane means no passing, and hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead are also no‑passing situations.

question: After several alcoholic drinks, the only thing that reduces the impairment is:
options: a:Drinking several cups of coffee.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Waiting several hours.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake, but they do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or restore safe driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to make a U-turn near a curve or hill?
options: a:When you cannot see clearly for at least 500 feet in each direction.,b:When you can see at least 500 feet in each direction.,c:When there are no vehicles behind you.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for a sufficient distance, typically at least 500 feet. Good visibility in both directions is required so you have enough time and space to complete the turn safely without surprising oncoming drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: After you pass, do not move back into the right lane until you can clearly see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting it off or forcing it to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you want to change lanes you should never:
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Move into another lane while within an intersection.
note: You should not change lanes while you are driving through an intersection because traffic and pedestrians may be crossing from several directions. Always wait until you are past the intersection, then signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and move into the new lane when it is safe.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of road rage incidents?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Use your horn frequently.
note: Signaling every lane change is a key way to prevent road rage because it lets other drivers know what you plan to do and reduces surprises. Clear communication and obeying traffic laws help avoid misunderstandings that can lead to anger or confrontations on the road.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also intend to turn right, you should:
options: a:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Large trucks and buses often need extra space and may swing wide to complete right turns. Never try to pass or squeeze between them and the curb. Instead, stay back and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its turn before you make yours to avoid being hit or trapped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane should you use to make a left turn from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: On a one-way street, a left turn should be made from the lane closest to the left curb because that lane lines you up directly with the turn and keeps you out of the path of traffic going straight or turning right. Always start your turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to yield your right-of-way?
options: a:Often, even at controlled intersections.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Never because it confuses other drivers.
note: Even if you technically have the right-of-way, you should yield whenever doing so helps prevent a collision. Insisting on your right-of-way when another driver is not yielding can lead to crashes; safety always comes before being “legally right.”

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you ever start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Never, you must not enter if you will block the intersection.,b:Only if cross traffic is light.,c:Only if you can completely clear the intersection before the light changes.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Blocking the intersection when the light changes can trap cross traffic and is illegal in many places. Only proceed on green when you are sure you can get all the way through without stopping in the intersection.

question: Which precaution is important when driving at night?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night your ability to see and judge distances is reduced, so you need more space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra time to see hazards and stop smoothly. Use low or high beams appropriately, and never stare into oncoming headlights.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in the fog.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan: look ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors every few seconds. This helps you spot hazards early and know what is happening behind and beside you. Do not stare at one spot, and never use high beams in fog because they reflect off the moisture and reduce visibility.

question: What is the only way to lower BAC and reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drinking caffeinated beverages.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Allowing time for the body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only time will sober you; nothing you eat or drink can speed up alcohol elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What steps should you take before changing lanes or passing?
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:Both of the above.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, always signal early to communicate your intentions, then check your mirrors and turn your head to check blind spots. Move only when you are sure the lane is clear and you have enough space.

question: What is the correct response to a sudden tire blowout?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the road edge.
note: In a tire blowout, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and steer straight. Do not brake hard. Ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually, then when it is under control, apply the brakes lightly and move out of the traffic lane to a safe place.

question: You should avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:
options: a:Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: On a multilane road, a solid yellow line beside a dashed yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Where a solid and a dashed yellow centerline appear together, traffic adjacent to the dashed line may cross to pass; traffic adjacent to the solid line may not.

question: Slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events typically:
options: a:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Causes traffic congestion.
note: 'Rubbernecking' creates slowdowns and congestion and can cause additional collisions; keep moving safely.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Traffic control devices.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Areas that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that cannot be seen by using the mirrors alone; check over your shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you go in the arrow's direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:After first coming to a complete stop.,c:Only after waiting for the light to change.
note: A green arrow allows movement in the arrow's direction from the proper lane when the way is clear; yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: How should you brake on snow or ice if your vehicle has ABS?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: In a vehicle equipped with ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and keep steady pressure on it. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and help you maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself, and do not rely on coasting to a stop on snow or ice when you need to slow or stop.
